entities.summary:
Hidulf was a renowned abbot and founder of Moyenmoutier Abbey, a prominent Benedictine monastery in Western Europe, active during the early Middle Ages. 

    Born in unknown dates, Hidulf's life is marked by his significant contributions to the Christian faith and his influence on the development of Western Europe. His most notable achievement is the founding of the Moyenmoutier Abbey, which became a major center of learning and spirituality. 

    Hidulf's legacy extends beyond his monastery, as he played a crucial role in the spread of Christianity throughout Western Europe. His reputation as a learned and pious individual led to his canonization as a saint by both the Catholic and Orthodox churches. 

    In commemoration of his feast day, July 11th, the Catholic Church recognizes Hidulf as a revered figure in the annals of Christian history, and his influence can still be felt in the modern-day institutions and traditions that continue to evolve from his foundation.
